questions.question_text: A converging lens is thicker at the:
questions.explanation: Converging (convex) lenses are thicker in the middle.

questions.question_text: A real image can be projected onto a screen because:
options: Light rays actually meet at the image point
Light rays only appear to meet
questions.correct_answer: Light rays actually meet at the image point
questions.explanation: Real images form where rays converge.

questions.question_text: Increasing the object distance beyond 2f for a converging lens makes the image:
questions.explanation: Beyond 2f the image is diminished and real.

questions.question_text: The lens formula relates focal length, object distance, and:
questions.explanation: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u connects f, image distance v, and object distance u.

questions.question_text: A diverging lens always forms a virtual, upright, diminished image.
questions.explanation: Diverging lenses spread rays; the image appears on the same side as the object.

questions.question_text: Decreasing the radius of curvature of a lens generally:
questions.explanation: A more curved surface gives a shorter focal length.

questions.question_text: When the object is placed at the focal point of a converging lens, the image is:
questions.explanation: Rays emerge parallel when the object is at F.

questions.question_text: Spectacles use lenses to correct vision by refracting light before it enters the eye.
questions.explanation: Lenses adjust where light focuses on the retina.

questions.question_text: Name the type of image that cannot be caught on a screen.
questions.explanation: Virtual images are formed where rays appear to diverge from.

questions.question_text: Write the lens formula using f, v, and u.
questions.explanation: Standard thin-lens equation.

questions.question_text: Gravitational force between two masses is proportional to:
questions.explanation: F = Gm₁m₂/r² shows proportionality to m₁m₂.

questions.question_text: Doubling the distance between two masses changes the force to:
questions.explanation: Force follows an inverse-square law with distance.

questions.question_text: If both masses are doubled while distance stays the same, the force becomes:
questions.explanation: F ∝ m₁m₂, so (2m)(2m) gives 4× force.

questions.question_text: Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation applies to:
questions.explanation: Gravity acts between all masses.

questions.question_text: Gravitational force is always attractive.
questions.explanation: Masses always attract; there is no repulsive gravity.

questions.question_text: Moving masses closer together:
questions.explanation: Smaller r gives larger F in F = Gm₁m₂/r².

questions.question_text: The gravitational force arrow in the simulation shows:
options: Direction and relative magnitude of force
questions.correct_answer: Direction and relative magnitude of force
questions.explanation: Force vectors indicate how strongly masses pull each other.

questions.question_text: Weight is the gravitational force on an object near a planet.
questions.explanation: Weight W = mg is the gravitational pull on mass m.

questions.question_text: Write Newton's law of gravitation as F = ...
questions.explanation: Force equals G times masses divided by distance squared.

questions.question_text: Name one quantity you can adjust with sliders in the simulation.
questions.explanation: Masses and separation distance can be adjusted.

questions.question_text: Hooke's Law states that spring force is proportional to:
questions.explanation: F = −kx relates force to displacement from equilibrium.

questions.question_text: Increasing the hanging mass on a spring generally:
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(m/k), so larger mass means longer period.

questions.question_text: A stiffer spring (larger k) with the same mass has:
questions.explanation: Higher k increases restoring force, increasing frequency.

questions.question_text: During oscillation, energy exchanges between:
questions.explanation: Energy shifts between KE and spring PE in SHM.

questions.question_text: For small oscillations, period does not depend on amplitude.
questions.explanation: Ideal SHM period is independent of amplitude.

questions.question_text: At the bottom of the oscillation (maximum stretch), velocity is:
questions.explanation: Turning points have zero velocity; energy is stored as PE.

questions.question_text: Simple harmonic motion is characterised by:
questions.explanation: SHM requires a restoring force ∝ displacement.

questions.question_text: Increasing amplitude increases maximum speed in SHM.
questions.explanation: More energy at larger amplitude means higher peak speeds.

questions.question_text: State Hooke's Law as an equation.
questions.explanation: Force is proportional to extension with negative sign for restoring direction.

questions.question_text: Name the motion of a mass on a spring after release.
questions.explanation: Spring-mass systems exhibit SHM for small displacements.

questions.question_text: Fluid pressure at a point in a liquid increases with:
questions.explanation: P = hρg shows pressure increases with depth.

questions.question_text: The formula for pressure in a fluid column is:
questions.explanation: Pressure equals depth × density × gravitational field strength.

questions.question_text: At the same depth, a denser fluid exerts:
options: The same pressure regardless of density
questions.explanation: Greater ρ means greater pressure at equal depth.

questions.question_text: Pressure in a fluid at rest acts:
options: Equally in all directions at a given depth
questions.correct_answer: Equally in all directions at a given depth
questions.explanation: Fluids transmit pressure uniformly at a level.

questions.question_text: Atmospheric pressure acts on the surface of an open liquid.
questions.explanation: Air pressure adds to the pressure measured in an open container.

questions.question_text: Moving the pressure sensor deeper in the same liquid:
questions.explanation: Deeper positions have higher hydrostatic pressure.

questions.question_text: Switching from water to honey at the same depth typically:
questions.explanation: Honey has higher density, so P = hρg is larger.

questions.question_text: Pressure depends on the shape of the container, not just depth.
questions.explanation: At a given depth in a connected fluid, pressure is the same regardless of container shape.

questions.question_text: Name one factor in P = hρg besides depth and g.
questions.explanation: Fluid density ρ determines pressure at a given depth.

questions.question_text: What instrument in the simulation measures pressure?
questions.explanation: The sensor reads pressure at chosen depths.

question_bank.title: Circuit Construction Kit: DC - Virtual Lab — Physics Assessment

questions.question_text: In a series circuit, the current through each component is:
questions.explanation: Series circuits have one path, so current is uniform.

questions.question_text: Increasing battery voltage in a simple resistor circuit generally:
questions.explanation: From Ohm's Law, higher V gives higher I for fixed R.

questions.question_text: An ammeter should be connected:
questions.explanation: Ammeters measure current and must be in series.

questions.question_text: A short circuit typically causes:
questions.explanation: Low-resistance paths allow dangerously large current.

questions.question_text: Ohm's Law states V = IR.
questions.explanation: Voltage equals current times resistance.

questions.question_text: Adding identical bulbs in series makes each bulb:
options: The same brightness as one alone
questions.explanation: Series adds resistance and shares voltage, reducing brightness.

questions.question_text: A voltmeter measures potential difference and is connected:
questions.explanation: Voltmeters measure voltage difference between two points.

questions.question_text: Kirchhoff's current law states that total current entering a junction equals total current leaving.
questions.explanation: Charge is conserved at circuit junctions.

questions.question_text: Name one measuring tool available in the virtual lab.
questions.explanation: Ammeters and voltmeters are used to measure circuit quantities.

questions.question_text: What happens to bulb brightness if resistance in series increases?
questions.explanation: Higher total resistance reduces current and power to bulbs.
